name: Courbet
shortDescription: France's first dreadnought, tier III battleship with the largest secondary battery of her class, backed by tied-for-thickest armor, but held back by a below-average hit point pool, sluggish turret traverse, and near-worst detection at the tier.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: Unlimited charges, 15s action, 80s cooldown. Mid-pack reset for a tier III battleship, quicker than Wyoming's 20s but well behind Ishizuchi's 10s.

consumables.name: Repair Party
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 28s each at roughly 204 hp/s, about 5,700 hp per activation, close to 14% of her 41,000 hp pool. Weakest heal of the tier III battleships researched so far, only the premium Nassau's 177 hp/s is lower.

consumables.name: Enhanced Secondary Targeting
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 30s window, -50% secondary dispersion and +100% shell grouping, 160s cooldown. Stock numbers shared across the tier, but landing on the biggest secondary battery of any tier III battleship (22 guns) makes it worth more here than on any peer.

turrets.note: Wing turret fixed to the port side, can't traverse to starboard at all.
Wing turret fixed to the starboard side, mirrors Turret 3.

strengths: 22-gun secondary battery is the largest of any tier III battleship researched, ahead of Wyoming, Orion, Ishizuchi, Nassau, and Gangut, all of which top out at 16
400mm max armor ties the premium Nassau for the thickest of the group, ahead of Kaiser's 350mm, Wyoming/Orion/Gangut's 305mm, and Ishizuchi's 254mm
8,300 AP damage ties Wyoming for second in the peer group, behind only Orion's 9,500, and matches her own "Superior AP Damage" trait
580m turning circle beats Kaiser's 600m, Wyoming's 590m, and Orion's 610m, and Ishizuchi's 740m by a wide margin; only Nassau's 510m turns tighter
12.3s upgraded rudder shift ties Orion for second-quickest of the group, beaten only by Nassau's 11.2s
weaknesses: 41,000 hp upgraded trails every tech-tree tier III battleship but Gangut's 37,600
60s to swing the main battery 180 degrees, the ship's own "Sluggish Aim" trait flags this as below-average traverse and it shows in a turning gunfight
12.8 km sea detection is worse than every peer but Ishizuchi's 12.9 km; Gangut spots first at 12.0 km, Nassau at 11.5 km
10% torpedo damage reduction beats only Ishizuchi's 4% and Gangut's 9%, every other peer sits at 13% or higher
21 kt upgraded beats only Gangut's 20.7 and Wyoming's 20.5, every other peer tops 22.7
Two of six turrets are fixed one to a broadside, so a full 12-gun salvo never happens, the best any single side gets is 10 guns
tips: Don't expect all six turrets on one broadside, only one of the two wing turrets can ever bear on a given side, so plan your approach around 10 guns, not 12
Lean into the secondary battery. With 22 guns and Enhanced Secondary Targeting, closing the range punishes the enemy more than it punishes you
That 60s traverse means you can get out-turned in a knife fight, so commit to an angle early instead of trying to track a flanking target
You'll usually be seen before you see them, so use the tight turning circle to dodge incoming fire rather than trying to out-spot anyone
Watch for torpedoes more than most tier III battleships, 10% damage reduction won't save you from a spread

threats.reason: Weak torpedo protection and near-worst detection at the tier make her an easy first target for a torpedo run.

threats.threat: Anything that can sit off her bow or stern in a turning fight
threats.reason: 60s main battery traverse means she can't track a target that keeps circling outside her broadside.

summary: France's first dreadnought, built around a massive 22-gun secondary battery rather than raw speed or armor scheme.
Twelve 305mm guns with above-average AP damage, but two of the six turrets are locked to one broadside each, so a full salvo tops out at 10 guns.
Tied-for-thickest armor and the tightest turning circle of her tech-tree peers, undercut by a below-average hit point pool and sluggish turret traverse.
Near-worst detection in both dimensions among her tech-tree tier III peers.
playstyle.detail: Courbet was the first battleship-dreadnought France built, and Legends carries over the awkward, transitional layout that came with it: six turrets at a single deck level instead of clean superfiring pairs, with the two wing turrets welded to one broadside each. That costs her a genuine 12-gun salvo, but the 22-gun secondary battery she carries instead is unmatched at the tier, and her 305mm AP shells hit hard enough to overmatch thin-plated targets outright, though at range they don't always carry enough velocity left to arm before punching through. She turns tighter than nearly everything else at the tier, which helps cover for a main battery that swings dead slow, but she gives up a chunk of her own hit point pool and gets spotted before most of her peers do. Play her like a brawler with reach: use the guns to soften someone at range, then let the secondaries finish the job once they close in.
